prompt: Write binary search as a recursive method that halves an index range instead of looping. Complete indexOf and searchRange, then run the tests.
explanation: Passing lo and hi as parameters is what lets recursion replace the loop: each call shrinks the range and hands the smaller problem to itself. The base case lo > hi means the range is empty, so the target is absent and -1 travels back up the call chain. Computing mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 avoids the integer overflow that (lo + hi) / 2 can hit on very large ranges, and recursing on mid + 1 or mid - 1 -- never mid itself -- guarantees progress toward the base case.
hints: Write the base case first: if lo > hi the range is empty, so return -1.
Compare sorted[mid] with target: equal means you are done, smaller means the target can only be to the right (mid + 1 .. hi), larger means to the left (lo .. mid - 1).
indexOf is a one-liner: return searchRange(sorted, target, 0, sorted.length - 1) -- which is already correct for an empty array, since 0 > -1.
